questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A utility-maximising consumer spends the whole of his disposable income of $40 on food and clothing. The table shows the price of food, the quantity purchased by the consumer, and the marginal utility he derives from food consumption. food price per unit $5 quantity demanded 5 marginal utility (units) 10 His marginal utility from clothing is 2 units. What is the price of clothing per unit and the quantity purchased by the consumer? clothing price quantity ($) (units)
For the purposes of measuring the income effect of a change in the price of a good, what is not held constant?

options.A: consumer preferences
options.B: relative prices
options.C: the consumer’s money income
options.D: the consumer’s real income

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the total product of labour (TPL) curve for a firm whose only variable factor input is labour. TPL total product of labour O number of workers employed What explains the shape of the curve?

options.A: diminishing marginal disutility of work
options.B: increasing marginal disutility of work
options.C: technical diseconomies of scale
options.D: the law of variable proportions

questions.questionText: A firm operates under perfect competition in both product and factor markets with labour as the only variable factor input. In the diagram, the line JK shows the relationship between the marginal physical product of labour and the hours worked: J marginal physical 6 product of labour (units) 4 K 0 1 2 3 4 5 thousand hours When the price of the product is $1.60, the firm uses 3000 hours of labour. What is the hourly wage?

The diagram shows an individual’s supply of labour curve. S w x z hourly wage ($) 40 y number of hours He is offered a job which would require him to work a standard 40-hour week. Which area measures the lowest amount he would have to be paid per week to get him to accept this job offer?

options.A: w + z B x + y C x + y - z D w + x + z + y

questions.questionText: What relationship does a firm’s long-run production function describe?

options.A: the firm’s output and the quantities of factor inputs employed
options.B: the firm’s long-run average cost of production and the level of output
options.C: the firm’s long-run average cost of production and the quantities of factor inputs employed
options.D: the prices of factor inputs and the quantities of factor inputs employed

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm’s total and marginal costs. output total cost ($) marginal cost ($)

A firm experiences external diseconomies of scale and decreasing returns to scale. How would these changes be illustrated on a cost curve diagram? shift in long-run movement along long- average cost curve run average cost curve

options.A: downward downward
options.B: downward upward
options.C: upward downward
options.D: upward upward

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a firm’s product. price D O quantity Which diagram depicts the shape of the firm’s corresponding total revenue (TR) curve?

options.A: B C D TR TR revenue revenue revenue revenue TR TR O O O O quantity quantity quantity quantity

questions.questionText: The firms in an industry all produce a homogeneous product, but each firm is able to influence the price it charges for its own product. In which market structure do the firms operate?

options.A: perfect competition
options.B: monopolistic competition
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: monopoly

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a monopoly. MC AC cost, revenue MR AR O X output What is the firm’s objective if it produces output OX?

options.A: to achieve normal profit
options.B: to maximise profit
options.C: to maximise total revenue
options.D: to minimise average cost

questions.questionText: The table shows information about a profit-maximising firm. price per unit $1.70 fixed costs $10000 variable costs per unit $1.75 What can be concluded about the firm’s behaviour?

options.A: It should close down immediately because it is not covering its average costs.
options.B: It should close down immediately because it is not covering its variable costs.
options.C: It should continue production in the long-run because it is covering its total costs.
options.D: It should continue production in the short-run because it is covering its fixed costs.

questions.questionText: When will a society have achieved an equitable distribution of income?

options.A: when all individuals have equal job opportunities
options.B: when all workers are paid wages equal to their marginal value product
options.C: when the incomes within the society are equally distributed
options.D: when the society believes that the distribution of income is fair

questions.questionText: The government introduces a minimum wage above the equilibrium market wage rate. How will this affect low-paid workers?

options.A: All those initially in employment will receive the new guaranteed minimum wage.
options.B: Fewer of those not already in employment will enter the labour force.
options.C: There will be an increase in the number of low-paid workers in employment.
options.D: Some low-paid workers will lose their job.

questions.questionText: A country’s steel producers are members of a cartel. Each member is allocated a production quota and initially produces the maximum allowed under its quota. What will be the effect on productive efficiency and on the industry’s profits if the producers are allowed to trade the quotas amongst themselves? effect on effect productive on profits efficiency

options.A: improvement increase
options.B: improvement no change
options.C: no change increase
options.D: no change no change

questions.questionText: Which government policy would not be classified as regulation?

options.A: bans on heroin and cocaine consumption
options.B: compulsory wearing of seatbelts in cars and coaches
options.C: licences for the extraction of water from lakes and rivers
options.D: taxation of cigarettes and tobacco products

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, the money supply in an open economy will increase if

options.A: domestic banks increase their lending to foreign borrowers.
options.B: the central bank buys foreign currency in the foreign exchange market.
options.C: the government sells bonds to domestic residents.
options.D: there is an increase in the volume of imports to the economy.

questions.questionText: Which is not an injection into a country’s circular flow of national income?

options.A: inward direct investment by multinational corporations
options.B: private gross domestic fixed capital formation
options.C: the sale of government bonds to members of the public
options.D: wages paid to civil servants

questions.questionText: The national income is initially in equilibrium. If there is an increase in exports, which change of equivalent value will restore national income to its initial equilibrium level?

options.A: a decrease in imports
options.B: a decrease in investment
options.C: an increase in government expenditure on goods and services
options.D: a reduction in taxation

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, investment increases by $400. At the new equilibrium level of income, consumption has increased by $1200. What is the value of the investment multiplier?

options.A: 2 B 3 C 4 D 8

questions.questionText: Assuming a constant income velocity of circulation of money, if the price level increases by 5% and the money supply grows by 2%, what will be the approximate change in real output (transactions)?
Why will an inflationary process be brought to a halt if the money supply is held constant?

options.A: Consumption will decrease as money incomes decline.
options.B: Government expenditure will have to be reduced as government revenues decline.
options.C: The rate of interest will rise as more money is required for transactions purposes.
options.D: The stimulus to invest will decline as the real burden of company debt rises.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the determination of the rate of interest in the economy, where M represents the money supply and LP represents liquidity preference. LP LP M

An economy is experiencing economic growth. What will be the effect on its rate of inflation, level of unemployment and current account surplus? level of current account rate of inflation unemployment surplus

options.A: lower lower lower
options.B: raise lower raise
options.C: raise raise uncertain
options.D: uncertain uncertain uncertain

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a country’s production possibility curve and a number of alternative production points. X U V capital goods Y Z O consumer goods Which change in the country’s output would be most likely to lead to a fall in potential growth?

options.A: U to V B U to X C Y to X D Y to Z

questions.questionText: A developing country receiving foreign financial aid is most likely to experience economic growth in the long-run if it uses the money to

options.A: boost welfare benefits for the poorest households.
options.B: pay for imports of capital goods.
options.C: reduce environmental pollution.
options.D: reduce income tax for all households.

questions.questionText: Increased borrowing by the government results in higher interest charges and this leads to less private investment expenditure. Of what is this an example?

options.A: an automatic stabiliser
options.B: crowding out
options.C: the accelerator
options.D: the substitution effect

questions.questionText: The data below relate to a particular country for the four years shown: Year 1 2 3 4 real GNP/head (Year 1 = 100) 100 110 121 121 life expectancy at birth (years) 65 64 65 67 % of age group enrolled in secondary 40 38 42 42 education What can definitely be concluded from these data?

options.A: Economic growth between Year 2 and Year 3 was 11%.
options.B: The level of economic development was better in Year 2 than in Year 1.
options.C: There was both economic growth and an improvement in economic development between Year 2 and Year 3.
options.D: No conclusions can be drawn as to whether the level of economic development was better in Year 4 than Year 3.

questions.questionText: A government’s budget is balanced at a time when the economy is fully employed, but an aggregate demand shock causes a decline in national income. What will be the result if the government keeps its tax rates and level of spending unchanged?

options.A: a cyclical budget deficit
options.B: a cyclical budget surplus
options.C: a structural budget deficit
options.D: a structural budget surplus reasonable effort has been made by the publisher (UCLES) to trace copyright holders, but if any items requiring clearance have unwittingly been included, the publisher will be pleased to make amends at the earliest possible opportunity.
